title: Investment Compliance Analyst
why_fit: Guideline-monitoring role in Investment Operations; maps to his Northrop model audits and internal-controls work, no experience minimum stated.
why_us: Wellington's Investment Operations team checks trades and holdings against client guidelines, and the Sentinel monitoring system is the core of this job. At Northrop Grumman I audited 100+ financial models for accuracy, compliance and internal controls, so reading rules and testing whether the numbers follow them is work I have done. At AMG I built a Python reconciliation that flags underpaid claims, which is the same habit of catching exceptions early. I want that kind of controls role at an asset manager, in Boston.
cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Investment Compliance Analyst role on Wellington's Investment Operations team. The work of reviewing investment management agreements, translating client guidelines into rules in Sentinel, and resolving post-trade exceptions is controls work, and controls work is where my background is strongest.

At Northrop Grumman, I audited more than 100 financial models for accuracy, compliance and internal controls. That meant reading what a model was supposed to do, testing whether it did it, and documenting the gaps. I also used SAP and Deltek Cobra to track program costs and keep the data clean, and I presented cost-saving recommendations to senior leadership.

At AMG Family Dental, I run financial operations for a practice serving more than 1,000 patients a year. I automated our weekly insurance payment reconciliation in Python, which cut processing time from 5 hours to 1 and flagged underpaid claims for follow-up. That process caught problems on a schedule instead of after the fact, which is the same idea as pre-trade support and post-trade exception review. Improving reporting and reconciliation in Dentrix also led me to recover more than $500K in annual revenue.

I hold an M.A. in International Economics and Finance from Brandeis and a B.S. in Business Administration with a Finance major from Suffolk. I am comfortable in Excel, SQL and Python, and I have used Bloomberg Terminal. The posting says prior guideline monitoring experience is helpful but not required, and I am ready to learn the equity, fixed income and derivative products behind the guidelines.

I live in the Boston area, can work in the office four days a week, and am available immediately. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your investment teams.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian

title: Client Service Representative - Alternatives

why_us: This role sits on BBH's alternatives fund accounting and administration side, working with fund accounting, reporting and client deliverables for private funds. My reconciliation work at AMG, where I automated a weekly insurance payment match in Python and went from 5 hours to 1, is the kind of accuracy-under-deadline work the posting describes. I also like that it is entry level with direct client contact, since I have presented to senior leadership at Northrop and want to build deeper fund accounting skills in Boston.
cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

The posting describes an entry-level role that supports client relationships across fund accounting, administration and custody, with a focus on accuracy, reporting and responsiveness. That combination fits the work I have done and the direction I want to take.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian

title: Client Analyst, Officer
why_fit: Client-facing analyst role in asset servicing; business-degree fit and Excel/reporting skills, but scope is client service rather than core finance analysis, so listed as Stretch.
why_us: State Street's Client Analyst role puts me between institutional clients and the teams that service their accounts, which needs accuracy under deadlines and comfort talking to clients. At AMG I track revenue and follow up on underpaid claims until they are resolved, and at Northrop I presented recommendations to senior leadership. I want to apply that follow-through and finance training at a global custodian headquartered in Boston. My Brandeis finance training and Excel, SQL and Python skills would support the analysis.
cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Client Analyst, Officer role at State Street in Boston. The posting asks for someone who can manage a workload independently, escalate issues at the right time, work well in a deadline-driven team and speak directly with clients. I have built those habits in my finance roles, and I want to bring them to an asset servicing business.

At AMG Family Dental, I direct financial operations for a practice serving more than 1,000 patients a year. I oversee billing, collections and revenue tracking, and I build the annual budget and monthly forecasts. By improving financial reporting and reconciliation in Dentrix, I found and recovered more than $500K in annual revenue. I reduced A/R aging by 10% by streamlining claim submission and following up on every open item. I also automated the weekly insurance payment reconciliation in Python, cutting the work from 5 hours to 1 and flagging underpaid claims. Each of these meant owning a queue of items, prioritizing them and closing them out.

At Northrop Grumman, I audited more than 100 financial models for accuracy, compliance and internal controls and presented cost-saving recommendations to senior leadership. That experience taught me to explain findings clearly and to escalate when something does not reconcile.

My education is an M.A. in International Economics and Finance from Brandeis and a B.S. in Business Administration with a Finance major from Suffolk. I work daily in Excel and am also comfortable with SQL and Python. I recognize that this role is more client-facing than my past positions, and I see that as a chance to broaden my skills.

I live in the Boston area and am available immediately. Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
